clue.text: Part of the WI fusses after cutting remark

indicators.note: after places the fusses behind the cutting remark in the answer

parts.note: a barb is a hurtful, cutting remark
ados are fusses or bothers

explanation.surface: Someone makes a cutting remark and the West Indies cricketers kick up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: WI is the standard abbreviation for the West Indies.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbados is one of the island nations of the Caribbean grouping known as the West Indies.

clue.text: Amphibian in a bunch salmon rises to swallow

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: to swallow says the first pieces take the bunch inside them
in a down clue, rises says the word for salmon is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: lox is smoked salmon
a lot is a bunch or group

explanation.surface: A frog-like creature lives among a shoal of salmon swimming upstream to feed.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rises' reads upwards, so backwards; 'to swallow' puts the bunch inside after the first O, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The axolotl is a Mexican salamander, a creature that lives in water and on land.

clue.text: Endlessly daring female — half- Scandinavian revolutionary

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for daring loses its final letter

parts.note: bold means daring
she is a female person

indicators.note: half says only the first half of the word for Scandinavian is kept

parts.note: a Viking was an early Scandinavian seafarer

explanation.surface: A bold woman with half-Scandinavian roots leads a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts BOLD to BOL and 'half-' cuts VIKING to VIK.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bolsheviks were the radical Russian faction led by Lenin, so one is a revolutionary.

clue.text: Old fool joins party, almost late

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: almost says the word for late lacks its final letter

parts.note: tardy means late

explanation.surface: An old buffoon turns up to a party, nearly late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TARDY to TARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A dotard is an elderly person whose wits have gone, a senile fool.

clue.text: Plant finally settled in stable location

definitions.meaning: a bulb-growing flower with white star-shaped blooms bears this name
the guiding light of the Nativity story came to rest over the stable where the infant lay

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs both to a white-flowered bulb and to the light the Magi followed to Jesus's birthplace.

clue.text: A frog, one metamorphosed into noted groom

indicators.note: metamorphosed means changed in form, so these letters change their arrangement

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A frog transforms into a famous bridegroom, like a fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metamorphosed' plays on frogs changing shape and on fairy-tale frogs becoming princes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's opera The Marriage of Figaro centres on the valet's wedding, making him a famous bridegroom.

clue.text: Lifting jug, drop round for a send-off

indicators.note: round says the word for drop goes around the other piece

parts.note: a fall is a drop

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting says the jug word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: an ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: Someone raises a jug and drops in for a farewell party.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'Lifting' reads the jug upwards; 'round' wraps the drop around it, and 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is a parting occasion, the send-off given to someone departing.

clue.text: State raised contribution from millionaire — gladly!

indicators.note: raised says the hidden letters are read backwards
contribution from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rich donor happily gives a contribution to a national cause.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means the run AIREGLA is read upwards, from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Algeria is a North African country, and a state is a nation.

clue.text: Dorothy confused about neat doctrine

indicators.note: about says the jumbled name wraps around the other piece
confused says the letters of the name are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
neat is an old word for cattle, a single one being an ox

explanation.surface: A muddled woman named Dorothy is unsure about some tidy teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' makes ORTHODY from DOROTHY, which goes 'about' OX; 'neat' meaning cattle is a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Orthodoxy is accepted belief or doctrine, the established teaching.

clue.text: Mixed bag in the post — sale offer?

parts.note: a post is a job or position
a lot is an item offered at an auction sale

explanation.surface: A miscellaneous parcel arrives in the mail, offered at a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' suggests mail, but here it means a position; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A job lot is a miscellaneous assortment sold together, a jumble of items.

clue.text: Unable to soak up the atmosphere

definitions.text: Unable to soak up the atmosphere

parts.words: Unable to soak up the atmosphere
parts.note: seems to describe someone who cannot enjoy a lively occasion, but literally means sealed so no air can get in

explanation.definitionFit: Something sealed against air cannot absorb any of the surrounding gas.

clue.text: Philanderer reluctant to have a port

parts.note: loth means reluctant or unwilling
taken as written
Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A womaniser is unwilling to drink some port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' tempts as the drink, but it is a harbour city; 'to have' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a seducer of women, named after a rake in an eighteenth-century play.

clue.text: Odd character that is transposed in misspelt word

indicators.note: in places the swapped letters inside the respelt word
misspelt says the letters of the word are wrongly ordered

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: transposed says the two letters of the abbreviation swap places

parts.note: ie is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A peculiar person swaps letters around in a misspelt word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transposed' turns IE to EI, which goes 'in' WRDO, the anagram of WORD from 'misspelt'.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is a strange, eccentric person, an odd sort.

clue.text: Surviving with a bad back

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back says the word for bad is read in reverse

parts.note: evil means bad or wicked

explanation.surface: Someone is still going despite a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like the sore body part but turns EVIL into LIVE; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alive means still living, having survived.

clue.text: Carpeting in a Times political leader one ignored

parts.note: taken as written
x is the multiplication sign, read as times

indicators.note: ignored says the word for one is left out of the political word

parts.note: a minister is a leading politician in government
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A government leader is reprimanded in The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' suggests a dressing-down; Axminster is a woven carpet named after a Devon town. 'ignored' drops one I from the politician, and 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a type of machine-woven carpet, so it is a kind of carpeting.

clue.text: Accompanying notes too glib — a book needs revision

indicators.note: needs revision says these letters must be rewritten in a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A book's notes are too slick and need rewriting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs revision' rearranges TOOGLIBAB.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, an obbligato is an instrumental part that accompanies the main melody.

clue.text: Soldier embraces a risque Italian hero

indicators.note: embraces says the soldier word goes around the other pieces

parts.note: GI is a US enlisted soldier
taken as written
ribald means bawdy or risque

explanation.surface: A soldier hugs a bawdy Italian patriot.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi led the fight for Italian unification and is revered as a national figure.

clue.text: Stun rhino on the rampage, circling round big rock

parts.note: KO, a knockout, means to stun

indicators.note: circling says the jumbled letters go around the round shape
on the rampage says the rhino letters run wild into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
o is round in shape

explanation.surface: A rampaging rhino must be stunned as it circles a large boulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rampage' turns RHINO into HINOR, which goes 'circling' O after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Koh-i-Noor is a huge diamond in the British Crown Jewels, and rock is slang for a diamond.

clue.text: One soon gives new issue a bit of bite

definitions.text: One soon gives new issue a bit of bite

parts.words: One soon gives new issue a bit of bite
parts.note: reads like praise of a fresh publication, but describes a first tooth that grows in a baby, new issue being offspring, and soon gives way

explanation.definitionFit: Children cut their first set of teeth in infancy, and these soon fall out.

clue.text: Youngster keeps map showing where Santa lives?

indicators.note: keeps says the youngster word holds the map word inside

parts.note: a lad is a youngster
a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: A boy holds a map showing the way to Father Christmas's home.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as legend rather than fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular tradition places Father Christmas's home in the far north of Finland.

clue.text: Money unexpectedly found in a boat, perhaps

definitions.meaning: slang for an unearned bonus or windfall
a sauce poured from a jug-like serving dish at dinner

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an easy windfall of cash and the meat sauce served from a sauce boat.

clue.text: Substitute leads All Blacks meeting a town in Italy

parts.note: vice means a deputy or substitute, as in vice-captain
the All Blacks are the New Zealand rugby team, NZ
taken as written

explanation.surface: A replacement leads the New Zealand rugby side against an Italian town.
explanation.walkthrough: The All Blacks are New Zealand's national rugby union team; 'leads' and 'meeting' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicenza is a city in the Veneto region of north-eastern Italy.

clue.text: Leave ice out of sweet drink

indicators.note: leave ice out of says the word ice is dropped from the word for the sweet

parts.note: liquorice is a black chewy sweet
the instruction to leave ice names those three letters as the ones to let go

explanation.surface: Take the ice out of a sweet drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes ICE from LIQUORICE, leaving the drink; a candy in American English is a sweet in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquor is alcoholic drink, especially spirits.

clue.text: New Oriental comrade, one from Asian kingdom

parts.note: E stands for east, and oriental means eastern
a pal is a friend or comrade
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A new eastern friend comes from a kingdom in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The Himalayan state was a kingdom when this was set.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepali means belonging to Nepal, the Himalayan country that was then ruled by a king.

clue.text: Relaxed face's enigmatic expression

indicators.note: enigmatic expression warns that the answer is a riddle, to be read as an instruction that rebuilds the clue word

parts.note: a clock face is a dial; the answer taken as an instruction turns the first word round to spell that dial, and enigmatic expression flags the riddle

explanation.surface: A calm person wears an inscrutable look.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay and it puts LAID backwards to give DIAL, a word for face.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid-back means easygoing and unhurried, calm in manner.

clue.text: Char employed by ministers needed drier

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
the cloth is a collective term for clergy or ministers of religion

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady working for the clergy needed a towel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' suggests a charwoman or cleaner, but is slang for tea; 'employed by' and 'needed' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea cloth is a towel used for drying dishes.

clue.text: Satellite channel is quiet, with zero backing in this country

indicators.note: in places the quiet letter and turned zero inside the country

parts.note: UK, the country where the paper is published
p, for piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: backing says the word for zero is read backwards

parts.note: nil means zero

explanation.surface: A satellite TV channel runs quietly, without British support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns NIL into LIN; 'is' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An uplink is the transmission path from a ground station up to a satellite.

clue.text: Director's less polite about his leading character

indicators.note: about says the less polite word goes around the letter

parts.note: ruder means less polite
his refers back to the director, whose first letter is D

explanation.surface: A film director is even ruder about the lead actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading character' suggests a star actor, but means the first letter of 'Director'; 's is is, a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rudder steers a ship, directing its course.

clue.text: Mum rushed about to do up part of Christmas cake

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: about says the word for rushed wraps around the fastening word

parts.note: ran means rushed
to zip is to fasten or do up

explanation.surface: Mother hurried around decorating the Christmas cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do up' looks like decorating but means fasten.
explanation.definitionFit: Marzipan is the almond paste layer beneath the icing of a traditional Christmas cake.
